en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l73.c13/:
Order!

Richard M Nixon, how do you plead on 1 count of treason against the United States of America, 1 count of misappropriation of campaign funds, 1 count of obstruction of justice, one count of abuse of power, one count of…

Richard Nixon, as he heard all this droning from the judge, closed his eyes, waiting for the sentence to end. He had been up all night, unable to sleep due to all the stress from the trial. Before he knew it, he’d fallen unconscious. All of a sudden, he jolted awake to the sound of the judge screaming; "NIXON! What do you plead?..."

"Uh, not guilty, your honour… not guilty?"

"On 1 count of sleeping in a court of law?..."

"When did you say tha- actually yes, your honour. The liberal media has been painting an askew picture of me. I was merely resting my eyes."
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l77.c14/:
Hubert Humphrey's inauguration address, January 20th, 1969.

Today I have stood, where once Abraham Lincoln stood and took an oath to my country. It is very appropriate then that from this bastion of America, this very heart of the great men who created the principles of freedom in this country, that today we sound the drum for freedom as have our generations of forebears before us done, time and time again through history. Let us rise to the call of freedom-loving blood that is in us and send our answer to the tyranny that clanks its chains upon the Negro. In the name of the greatest country that has ever trod this earth, I draw the line in the dust and toss the gauntlet before the feet of tyranny . . . and I say . . . desegregation today . . . desegregation tomorrow . . . desegregation forever!
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l93.c27/: The murders and rioting in America will be your first order of business, and more long term, the war on Vietnam. If both of those are dealt with, your silent majority will be pleased. Other than that, inflation must be dealt with, as well as the excess of Great Society. Good luck, and welcome back to the executive branch!
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l95.c32/: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your performance in debates and campaigning were widely praised compared to 1960, which allowed you to win with a massive landslide. What a turnaround from 1964!
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l97.c32/: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. Your lead dwindled a bit as Wallace’s appeal dampened, but your coalition managed to remain intact.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l100.c32: Congratulations! Despite the intense battle from Humphrey and Wallace, you have disproven the doubters and redeemed your name. The bombing halt and Wallace collapsing in the north nearly lost you the election, but you managed to hang on.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l103.c33: For the first time since 1888, the winner of the electoral vote lost the popular vote. It seems many people underestimated how much of an effect Wallace had on your campaign in the south.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l106.c27: After your second loss in a presidential election, your chances of being renominated for the presidency, or ANYTHING for that matter is nearly zero. Retirement and an elder statesman position are all that will await you. It seems Americans will once and for all not have Nixon to kick around…
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l108.c32: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 7 of the last 9 presidential elections. With the margins being as close as 8 years ago, you are already having flashbacks of 1960.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l111.c32: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Somehow you managed to do worse compared to 1960. Nobody is quite sure how that is even possible, but suffice it to say you will receive much of the blame.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l113.c32: Despite the environment seemingly being perfect for a Nixon comeback, you had a sudden and shocking reversal of fortunes, and have lost yet another presidential election. Republicans are shocked they have now lost 8 of the last 10 presidential elections. Not only did you lose, but you got crushed. Under the weight of two ideologically different candidates, your moderate positions seemed to not appeal. If the skirmish between liberal and conservative republicans wasn’t already bad, it was going to get a lot worse after this.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l117.c33: At the end of the day, in possibly the most shocking turn of events, the popular vote fell in your favour. Nobody is sure what to make of this, but maybe the Democrats can use their house and senate supermajorities, combined with disaffected Republicans, to pass electoral reform?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l122.c27: A return to the Senate might be in order, so you might defend liberalism from demise during Nixon's administration, or gearing up for a run in 1972. perhaps you can do both. In any case, let's hope Nixon can cool tensions in America and bring the troops home.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l124.c32: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. You still fought hard, and took Nixon to the brink as Kennedy did in 60.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l126.c32: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. The crime and rioting took a toll on your campaign hard, and Nixon's law and order theme really hit home for many Americans.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l128.c32: Despite your best efforts in a tough climate, Richard Nixon will succeed Johnson in the presidency. It was always going to be difficult being so closely associated with an unpopular administration, in a divided party. It seems liberalism very well might be over with this loss, as you have been crushed. A more moderate candidate in 4 years will likely be chosen.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l131.c27: Your first course of action is to fix what Johnson caused. Vietnam and the riots need to be dealt with. Johnson might not like how you deal with it, but this is your administration, and you'll deal with it the way you do. Act quickly, or you just might become as unpopular as Johnson.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l133.c32: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. To the shock of pundits countrywide, you beat Nixon and Wallace handily. The bombing halt and your inspiring words compared to Nixon must have won it for you.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l135.c32: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. It seems America is ready to give the New Deal Democrats one last chance. If you succeed, you might be able to rebuild the coalition that's won them so many elections (well, not the Deep South, but you knew that).
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l137.c32: The happy warrior rises! Despite a climate of chaos and a split in the Democratic Party, you've beaten back the opposition and secured a third term for the Democrats. Johnson breathes a sigh of relief after this, and poor Nixon is once again a loser. He did quite well, however, so you best work hard, lest the midterms act mercilessly.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l141.c23: As expected, you lost the 1968 election
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l142.c23: What happens next is your choice. Another governorship wouldn't hurt, and perhaps you can run again in 4 years if you're up to it. Unfortunately (for you), civil rights will persist.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l148.c32: In a shock to all parties involved, neither Hubert Horatio Humphrey nor Richard Milhous Nixon will be the next president of the United States. Somehow, you managed to come out on top. Southerners are ecstatic, liberals are foaming at the mouth, and the black population has never been more fearful.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l149.c31: Pundits are shocked, trying to figure out how you managed to capture states outside the deep south to win it all. What happens next is entirely unknown. Its likely a crusader against the civil rights bill will happen, as well as the deconstruction of Great Society, and the escalation of Vietnam. Whatever happens, sit back and relax knowing you've done the greatest upset in US political history!
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l152.c32: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You did, however, come very close, picking up a number of states you weren't expected to pick up. It seems that your crusade for the south turned out really well. You could run in four years perhaps, and try and win the same coalition, trying to deadlock the election then. You've sent a clear message to the Democrats; the south isn't to be ignored,
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l154.c32: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You did, however, poll a bit higher above what you were set to win. So good job outdoing your predictions. The south isn't done yet, as you've shown here.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/ending/s0.l156.c32: As most expected, you've lost. This isn't a surprise, as you're a third party. even worse, your second goal of deadlocking the electoral college failed. You won just about as much as expected, and yet it wasn't enough. Your supporters are disillusioned that you weren't able to deadlock the college. That's how it is, though...
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/334: What will be the overall message of your campaign?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/252: What is your overall position on the Vietnam War?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/255: Are you satisfied with this nation's economic performance over the previous five years?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/338: What is more important to you -- competing with Nixon in the border states (to help Humphrey) or winning over Humphrey voters in the northern cities (to help Nixon)?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/256: Are you satisfied with the progress of desegregation in this country since the passage of the Civil Rights Act of 1964?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/253: If elected, what will you do to get the student and Negro riots in this country under control?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/254: What is your opinion of Lyndon Johnson's new Medicare program?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/280: What is your opinion of the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965? Is it a good idea to liberalize our immigration policy and to outlaw national origin quotas?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/287: How would you prevent campus incidents like the takeover of Columbia University that occurred this past spring?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/273: Would you appoint federal judges who support the decision Engel v. Vitale outlawing mandatory school prayer?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/263: Some have proposed implementing an Environmental Protection Agency at the federal level to combat industrial pollution. Would you support this as President?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/272: What is your opinion on the legality of abortion? Would you attempt to legalize or prohibit this practice at the federal level?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/270: Are you concerned with some of the activist stances that Earl Warren has taken in his time with the Supreme Court?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/257: Would you be willing to call an unconditional bombing halt of North Vietnam in the hopes of restarting peace negotiations?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/271: Has the current Supreme Court contributed to our disorder with decisions such as Gideon v. Wainright and Miranda v. Arizona?

en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/335: Do you plan to make a strong effort in any of the non-Southern states?

en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/285: Do you support the Child Nutrition Act of 1966, which provides free breakfast and milk to qualified schoolchildren of impoverished backgrounds? Or do you believe that the program is too costly and constitutes a misuse of federal power?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/291: Do you believe that President Johnson overstepped his bounds in negotiating the Kennedy Round of trade agreements? Do you support the liberalization of international trade under the GATT?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/265: Should Lyndon Johnson have been able to prevent the Tet Offensive?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/275: What do you think of programs that require schools to use busing to achieve racial balance?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/340: If there is no majority in the electoral college, what are your goals at the bargaining table?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/questions_json/333: On the weekend before the election, Lyndon Johnson's peace negotiations have collapsed with the North Vietnamese. Even worse, there are rumors that a Nixon operative has sabotaged the negotiations. Nixon swears to you on his honor that he is innocent. Will you make this an issue over the last two days of the campaign?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1653@: We keep emboldening the enemy in Vietnam with half-measures. We will never win this war unless we escalate it.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1654@: I'm in no position to comment on the conduct of the war. When I'm President I will do everything in my power to seek peace, but I cannot undermine the current Administration.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1655@: We should stop bombing North Vietnam and attempt to negotiate a peace settlement. In the mean time, we should be putting our troops at risk only when absolutely necessary.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1656@: We need to pull our forces out of Vietnam as soon as possible. This war is a national disgrace.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1657@: There has been a total abdication of responsibility in this country over the past five years. The riots in Detroit and Newark are simply the final straw in what we can accept. I will crack down severely on disorder and nominate judges who will overturn atrocious decisions such as Miranda v. Arizona.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1658@: Law and order is the primary theme of my campaign. We also need to encourage investment in the ghettoes to ensure a high quality of life and prevent these occurrences.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1659@: Our first priority is always to have strong law enforcement. We also need more spending on education, more integration in our schools, and more programs to ensure that blacks can advance in our society after the stain of segregation.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1660@: If we had peace in Vietnam and more investment in education here at home, we wouldn't be having these riots.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1661@: Medicare is the first step towards socialized medicine in this country. We need to end this program as soon as possible and return health care to the states and to the people.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1662@: We need to be very cautious about this program. It's important to ensure that the indigent can receive care, but programs like these always run the risk of adding precipitously to our national deficit.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1663@: I commend this piece of legislation. Already we see many Americans receiving health care who would otherwise be stricken with serious and/or fatal conditions.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1664@: Medicare is only the beginning of what we need to do in this country. I support a national health care system for all Americans.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1665@: How can anyone be satisfied with the course our nation has taken? Inflation is killing the value of the dollar and the gold standard itself is at risk. Unemployment is highest under the Johnson Administration among the very people he claims to care about the most.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1666@: Our current economic path is not sustainable. We need to continue the growth we have seen but we cannot allow this inflation we have to continue.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1667@: The unemployment rate right now is under four percent. Workers, particularly those in labor unions, enjoy high purchasing power and an ever-expanding lifestyle. Economic growth throughout the 1960s has been outstanding.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1668@: The worst thing we can do right now is to sabotage the progress we have seen by continuing to squander our money on a war in Vietnam. I support a full employment economy as well -- meaning we must be vigilant against misguided attempts to raise interest rates.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1669@: Whites and Negroes are naturally unsuited to mix together in society. The entire premise of desegregation is a farce, and my campaign is dedicated to ending this misguided policy.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1670@: I strongly support what we have done to end the insidious practice of segregation in the South. However I'm also alarmed at some of the ideas I've heard about forced integration of neighborhoods, or the proposed busing of students to distant schools.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1671@: We have achieved great strides on this issue in the past twenty years -- and let the record show that Hubert H. Humphrey was at the forefront of this movement as early as 1948. We still have a long way to go, however, before we can truly realize the dream of Martin Luther King.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1672@: We need to be very aggressive in fighting racism and its effects where they exist. I support programs such as busing, affirmative action, the new HUD department, and anything else that is necessary to integrate all regions of the United States.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1673@: If anything, we need to escalate the bombing of North Vietnam. I don't go to bed at night with the feeling that they truly respect the power of America.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1674@: We will never win the peace in Vietnam by caving in to the Communists. I cannot support such an ill-conceived measure.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1675@: I would be willing to take this step and see what develops. It is imperative that we end the war in Vietnam as soon as possible.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1676@: We need to pull our forces out of Vietnam as soon as possible. This war is a national disgrace.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1685@: We should always be wary of the corruption inherent in these large unions. I cannot say that I'm a supporter of the AFL-CIO.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1686@: Every man should have a choice on whether to join a union or not. These large outfits monopolize the work force and use their power to perpetrate voter fraud and to enrich their bosses.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1687@: The AFL-CIO is a centerpiece of the great American bargain. Our economy can never thrive unless the people who work to keep it going thrive as well. I fully support the AFL-CIO.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1694@: This is one of the most dangerous ideas I can think of. A federal agency to combat pollution will hurt business, increase unemployment, and undermine the wages of our workers.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1695@: I believe that existing government agencies can handle the issues we have. It does upset any decent American to see rivers filled with black sludge and industrial waste.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1696@: This is something I whole-heartedly support. We have rivers that are unusable to humans, acid rain falling from the skies, and smog so thick in some cities that people can barely see.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1700@: The Tet Offensive was an absolute disaster for the North Vietnamese. Why should it have been prevented?
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1701@: I'm worried that for most or all of 1967, Lyndon Johnson repeatedly assured us that the North Vietnamese were on their last legs. It's difficult to assess the situation when we can't rely on the information that we have.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1702@: We should have had greater security in those places where we were attacked. Let us not forget, however, that this attack greatly hurt the Viet Cong and was a victory for the United States.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1703@: We could have prevented the Tet Offensive entirely if we'd never entangled ourselves in this Vietnamese quagmire.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1720@: Earl Warren is without a doubt the worst Supreme Court justice in the history of the United States. From Brown v. Board of Education up through the present day, he has been nothing but an agent of tyranny for the federal government.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1721@: On the balance I would not appoint another justice like Mr. Warren. Desegregating our schools was one thing, but he has gone off the deep end on these issues like school prayer, Miranda rights, and other activist decisions.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1722@: It would be better in some cases if we could get Congress to make these decisions, but I do support the stances Mr. Warren has taken on the Court.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1723@: The Warren Court is the first Supreme Court in history which has had the guts to use constitutional law for the benefit of the common citizen. I will continue to appoint sound judges like Mr. Warren, Abe Fortas, and Thurgood Marshall.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1724@: Over the past five years we've sent a message to criminals that their rights are more important than the rights of law-abiding Americans. I don't know how anyone was surprised at the rioting and social chaos that we've seen since then.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1725@: My priority as President will be to fight for law and order in this country. The Court had good intentions but I am concerned that they overstepped their bounds in these cases.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1726@: Due process for defendants is a Constitutional right. I'm confident that we will find a way to enforce the law in this country without devolving into a police state.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1727@: Abortion is an evil, murderous practice. I will stand firm against any attempts to protect this barbarism at the federal level.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1728@: We all have our own opinions on this practice, but I think the current system is the one that we should stay with. The individual states should be allowed to legislate on abortion as they so please.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1729@: I'm opposed to the practice of abortion personally, but I would support a federal law protecting access to this procedure in the most dire cases for the woman, such as when her life or health are in danger.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1730@: I support the right of women to control their reproductive destiny. This should be defended at the federal level.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1731@: This decision was atrocious. I don't think it's an exaggeration to say that our way of life is at stake here when we don't allow our schools to teach basic moral values to our children.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1732@: I was disappointed with this decision. I would certainly appoint judges who see the wisdom in teaching our kids a few lessons about morality.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1733@: We have Catholics, Jews, and others in this country who should not be forced to pray in a certain way because of what some principal believes in a public school. This is a First Amendment issue in my opinion.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1734@: I will appoint judges who support religious freedom in the United States. Absolutely.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1738@: Busing is nothing but another conspiracy to mongrelize the races of this country. First it was the Brown decision. Now it's some policy that some academic came up with to send children to school thirty miles from their house as part of some social engineering scheme.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1739@: I stand opposed to the legal segregation of our schools. Legal segregation promotes inferior education. I also think that busing promotes inferior education. My goal is to see every child in this country get a good education.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1740@: I do agree with the idea that education is a local matter. I'm not especially opposed to busing where local authorities deem it necessary, but I would only use the federal government in extraordinary circumstances.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1741@: What good is a Court decision banning segregation if we don't actually do something to integrate our schools? People oppose busing because they oppose school integration, pure and simple.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1748@: Our inflation is being caused by all of this Great Society nonsense that Johnson passed. I will slash these programs, slash our deficits, and end our inflation problem overnight.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1749@: The inflation rate we have in this country speaks to the heart of the Democrats' problems in running the economy. They claim to be the party of the working man, but they are fine with debasing wages and property values with their misguided social engineering.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1750@: Right now we have the strongest economy almost in the history of the United States. Unemployment is at 3% and our national output is growing at a furious pace. Compared to this, our 4% inflation rate is a pretty minor concern.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1751@: The Republicans are grasping at straws with this inflation argument. They know that Kennedy and Johnson have managed the economy far better than Eisenhower, so they are resorting to the only argument they have left.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1756@: The Negro problem apparently wasn't enough for our federal bureaucrats, because they decided to add Mexicans and Orientals to the list as well. I oppose new immigration to this country.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1757@: We need to be vigilant on the amount of immigration that we allow, but I also agree that we shouldn't restrict the practice based on national origin. In a Cold War world, we need to be mindful of international perceptions.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1758@: This is a fair and sensible policy that will allow skilled immigrants to enter the United States. It's ludicrous to state that this will somehow compromise our culture and our values.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1759@: Our former immigration policy was a national embarrassment. This country was built by immigrants and my only complaint right now is that the overall number of visas is still far too low for our needs.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1764@: I wish we would have had the guts to intervene in Cuba the way we did in the Dominican Republic. I will do anything I can as President to prevent a Communist insurgency in Latin America.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1765@: With minimal cost and minimal loss of life, President Johnson was able to prevent a Communist uprising in the Dominican Republic. I fully support his actions in that area.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1766@: I do support the intervention. We also need to reexamine our policies in general towards Latin America to ensure higher economic growth and more political freedom there.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1767@: We have long supported right-wing government in the Dominican Republic, and we've now propped it up against the will of the people. We can't credibly claim to fight for democracy when we do things like this.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1774@: I don't think anyone opposes the idea of providing milk to our poor kids. My contention, however, is that the state and local governments are more in tune with their needs than some bureaucrats in Washington.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1775@: This is a sensible piece of legislation. I support it and I think that every decent American supports it too.
en.1968_Wallace_Thurmond/answers_json/1779@: How these students have not been expelled is beyond me. If Administrators want to be complicit in the degradation of a private university, that is their own business. However, I won't spend a dime of federal money on a school that coddles radical agitators.
